change.title: pr-1-flat
change.description: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on the audit log's datetime key
findings.body: The class copies `Paginator.get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor`, which expect a numeric key. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `getattr(item, 'datetime')` is a `datetime`. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls this key function on the results, so every request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one row gets a 500. `DateTimePaginator` (paginator.py:233-241) converts the datetime to a timestamp multiplied by 1000. A non-empty `cursor.value` would also be passed unconverted into the `datetime <= %s` filter (line 843), which is also wrong. Subclass `DateTimePaginator`, or drop the new class.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing is unsupported by Django and the comments claim otherwise
findings.body: `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment at lines 876-879 says the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" and that the path "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". Both claims are false. The offset comes straight from the user-supplied cursor string. A client sending `optimized_pagination=true` and a negative offset gets a 500. If the slice were supported, the cursor would reach rows outside the cursor window. The 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' justification does not cover that. Remove the negative-offset branch. If efficient reverse pagination is the goal, it needs a real design, not a slice with a negative start.

findings.title: Unrelated behavior change in shared BasePaginator, with a misleading comment
findings.body: This edit applies to every `BasePaginator` subclass (Paginator, DateTimePaginator, and others), not just the audit log. For non-prev cursors, a negative offset is now clamped to 0 instead of failing. A tampered cursor then silently returns the first page rather than an error. For `is_prev` the offset is still used unclamped, so negative values still hit Django's assertion. The comment says negative offsets are being 'allowed', but the code does the opposite for non-prev cursors and nothing for prev cursors. Revert this hunk. If clamping is wanted, it should be a separate, tested change that also covers `is_prev`.

findings.title: New query-param gated code path, with no tests and an unclear access check
findings.body: The `optimized_pagination` flag switches the endpoint to a paginator that has no tests and is broken (see the findings on paginator.py). The gate `request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access` is not a meaningful boundary here. `OrganizationAuditPermission` already limits who reaches this endpoint, and the paginator offers no capability that needs a separate check. `is_superuser` is also not the same as an active superuser session. Remove the branch. Otherwise add tests for the optimized path and for the case where `organization_context.member` is None.

findings.title: get_result is a near-copy of BasePaginator.get_result
findings.body: The entire `get_result` is duplicated for one extra branch, so future fixes to the base method will diverge. If this class stays, override only the slicing step. Also note that line 891 still uses the raw `offset`, which is inconsistent with the negative-offset branch.

findings.title: Comment promises negative-offset support that the code does not provide
findings.body: `Cursor.__init__` only does `int(offset)`, as it did before, and nothing here makes negative offsets work. The comment is misleading for readers of this core class, so remove it.

contracts.action: Audit log GET with optimized_pagination=true routes to OptimizedCursorPaginator
contracts.before_after: The existing path converts the datetime key to a timestamp multiplied by 1000 (paginator.py:233-241). The new paginator reuses the numeric Paginator key function (paginator.py:838-843) on a datetime field.
contracts.visible_effect: Any non-empty result set returns a 500 with the flag on. A negative cursor offset also returns a 500, because Django rejects the negative slice.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError from math.floor(datetime) when the cursor is built. AssertionError on the negative slice start.

summary: Not mergeable. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` crashes on the audit log's datetime key, so the `optimized_pagination=true` path returns a 500 for any non-empty result. Its negative-offset slicing is unsupported by Django, so a negative cursor offset also fails with a 500. The comments claim the opposite. An unrelated clamp was added to the shared `BasePaginator`. The new path has no tests, and about 100 lines are copied from the base `get_result`. I only read the code and did not run it.
